findings.sourceEnglish: A staple earns its place because it feeds the household beyond the day of harvest.
findings.currentRegistryDraft: Tshiḽiwa tsha vhuthogwa [staple] tshi wana vhuimo hatsho ngauri tshi ṋea muṱa zwiḽiwa u fhirisa ḓuvha ḽa khaṋo.

findings.finding: Existing localized paragraph matches the current VE registry verbatim. No candidate change.

findings.sourceEnglish: It carries energy or protein. It stores, or it stays in the ground until you need it. And often it carries cultural memory too.
findings.currentRegistryDraft: Tshiḽiwa tsha vhuthogwa tshi fara energy kana protein. Tshi a vhulungea kana tshi sala tshi mavuni u swika ni tshi tshi ṱoḓa. Nahone kanzhi tshi na cultural memory.
findings.candidate: Tshiḽiwa tsha vhuthogwa tshi fara energy kana protein. Tshi a vhulungea kana tshi sala tshi mavuni u swika ni tshi tshi ṱoḓa. Nahone kanzhi tshi na cultural memory.
findings.finding: Existing localized paragraph matches the current VE registry verbatim. Its energy/protein, storage-or-stays-in-ground, and cultural-memory content is untouched.

findings.sourceEnglish: One staple leaves you vulnerable. Two or more give you options when weather or pests hit.
findings.currentRegistryDraft: Tshiḽiwa tshithihi tsha vhuthogwa tshi ni sia ni vulnerable. Zwiḽiwa zwa vhuthogwa zwivhili kana zwo engaho zwi ni ṋea khetho musi mutsho kana zwikhokhonono zwi tshi kwama zwimela.
findings.candidate: Tshiḽiwa tshithihi tsha vhuthogwa tshi ni sia ni vulnerable. Zwiḽiwa zwa vhuthogwa zwivhili kana zwo engaho zwi ni ṋea khetho musi mutsho kana zwikhokhonono zwi tshi kwama zwimela.
findings.finding: Existing localized paragraph matches the current VE registry verbatim; one staple vulnerability and two-or-more options under weather/pest pressure remain intact.

findings.sourceEnglish: Grow at least two. Not one.
findings.currentRegistryDraft: Grow at least two. Not one.
findings.candidate: Alusani zwivhili kana zwo engaho. Hu si tshithihi.
findings.finding: “Grow two or more. Not one.” preserves the threshold and contrast; no crop is added.

findings.sourceEnglish: Which staple does your household rely on most heavily right now? That's the one whose failure would hurt most — so that's the one that needs a companion.
findings.currentRegistryDraft: Which staple does your household rely on most heavily right now? That's the one whose failure would hurt most — so that's the one that needs a companion.
findings.candidate: Ndi tshiḽiwa tshifhio tsha vhuthogwa tshine muṱa waṋu wa ḓitika ngatsho vhukuma zwino? Ndi tshenetsho tshine u kundwa hatsho ha nga ni vhaisa vhukuma — ngauralo tshi ṱoḓa companion.
findings.finding: Two comparative/modal nuances are weakened: `vhukuma zwino` reads “very much now,” not necessarily “most heavily right now” among staples; the failure clause is backtranslated as “could hurt you most,” while draft wording says `ha nga ni vhaisa vhukuma` (“could hurt you very much”), losing “most.” Retain the two source sentences exact English until both comparative and “would hurt most” meaning can be expressed precisely.

findings.finding: Existing localized paragraph matches the current VE registry verbatim; distinct protection against different threats remains unchanged.

findings.currentRegistryDraft: Zwimela zwo fhambanaho zwi shumisa maḓi, mavu na khalaṅwaha nga nḓila dzo fhambanaho. That difference is the protection.

overall: Hold paragraph 4 exact English unless the source comparatives and counterfactual failure wording can be preserved precisely. Other candidates and holds preserve their stated source meaning at this semantic-check level. No fluent approval is claimed.
